facts.label: Descrever um lugar
facts.sub: Pergunte What’s it like there? e responda com It’s + adjetivo (warm, sunny, small). Para dizer o que existe, use We have + substantivo. Reaja com It sounds lovely.

facts.label: Cidade natal
facts.sub: Falar da cidade natal é um ótimo assunto para conhecer pessoas. Gente dos EUA costuma perguntar sobre clima, comida e coisas que se pode fazer por lá.

facts.label: Conversa sobre o clima
facts.sub: Falar do tempo é simples e simpático. Frases como “It’s warm and sunny” e “It’s cold in winter” são muito usadas em conversas rápidas.

compare.br: In Brazil, people often ask “De onde você é?” and share a few details about the city, the beach or the food.
compare.us: In the USA, small talk about hometowns includes weather, food and fun things to do. Short, positive answers are common.

pages.title: Two women, one rainy day · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a rainy afternoon in a cafe in Salvador. Two women sit at a small table near the door. Miriam is new in the city, and she loves to meet people. “**Where are you from?**” she asks the woman next to her.
“**I’m from Salvador, in Brazil,**” the woman answers. “**What’s it like there?**” asks Miriam. “**It’s warm and sunny all year,**” says the woman. “**Is it near the ocean?**” asks Miriam.

pages.title: Two women, one rainy day · 2/3
paragraphs: “**Yes, we have beautiful beaches,**” says the woman. “**What’s the food like?**” asks Miriam. “**Delicious! Rice, beans, and fish,**” says the woman. Her eyes are bright when she talks about home.

“**What do people do for fun?**” Miriam asks. “They play music, dance and go to the beach.” “My hometown is small, but it’s beautiful because it’s near the sea,” says the woman. Miriam listens and smiles.
